# URF/PWG qualification fixtures

This directory contains small Apple Raster (`image/urf`) inputs and the
metadata needed to qualify `internal/urf.Translate` against an independent
CUPS decoder.  The fixture bytes are generated by the Go program in
`cmd/generate`; the generator has no dependency on the production parser or
on CUPS.

The checked-in source reference is OpenPrinting CUPS **2.4.14**, tag-object
short ID `2190813d`.  This directory records that short ID, rather than
claiming a full commit hash; the referenced implementation is
[`cups/raster-stream.c` at v2.4.14](https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/blob/v2.4.14/cups/raster-stream.c).
The fixtures were generated and checked on macOS 27 with Apple CUPS
**2.3.4**:

```text
cups-config --version       # 2.3.4
/usr/libexec/cups/filter/rastertopwg
```

The system filters are an oracle only.  Normal Go tests do not invoke them or
require libcups, cgo, ImageMagick, or a printer.  To regenerate inputs and
the CUPS reference streams on a host with the filters installed:

```sh
# Run from the repository root.
internal/urf/testdata/generate.sh
```

To qualify the current translator implementation, including its normalized
PWG headers and decoded pixels, require the native CUPS reader explicitly:

```sh
go run ./internal/urf/testdata/cmd/qualify \
  -manifest internal/urf/testdata/manifest.json \
  -require-cups
```

The command first runs `urf.Translate` for every fixture, then calls
`cupsRasterOpen`, `cupsRasterReadHeader2`, and `cupsRasterReadPixels` through
the small Python `ctypes` oracle in `cmd/qualify/cups_oracle.py` on both the
translator output and the checked-in CUPS reference PWG stream.  It compares
every decoded page and every raw pixel byte (via SHA-256), and checks the
selected normative PWG header fields listed in the manifest.  This reads the
original PWG stream directly: it does not patch `CUPS_CSPACE_SW` and does not
route either stream through a TIFF converter.  Without Python/libcups, the
command reports a skipped qualification unless `-require-cups` is set.

`generate.sh` uses the native `rastertopwg` writer to create the checked-in
references and the same direct ctypes oracle to write one `.cups.json` header
and pixel digest beside each PWG stream.  This avoids a TIFF conversion path:
Apple CUPS 2.3.4's TIFF filter rejects PWG color space 18
(`CUPS_CSPACE_SW`), while the native CUPS reader accepts the unmodified
stream.  The native writer also supplies filter defaults (for example
`media_name`, `media_type`, total page count, image box, print quality, and
floating-point fields) that differ from the translator's policy header.
Qualification therefore compares pixels against the native reference and
compares the translator's policy fields against the independent CUPS reader,
rather than mistaking those filter defaults for the requested policy.

The `cups-permissive` fixtures intentionally exercise behavior accepted by
CUPS: clear-to-end-of-line (`0x80`), a repeated run beyond the remaining row
width, a literal run whose advertised length is clipped to the row width, and
a row repetition count beyond the page height.  CUPS also ignores the Apple
declared page count, reserved page-header bytes, partial/trailing bytes after
the last complete page, and extra pages past the count.  The package's
independent parser tests cover those header/trailing-byte cases; this
qualification command checks the generated permissive streams against the
native reader.

The translator follows CUPS for the Apple file header as well: it accepts the
`UNIR` sync word (and the `RINU` byte-order spelling) and ignores the remaining
eight file-header bytes.  A zero `Limits` field selects the finite package
default; the normal qualification fixtures use `DefaultLimits` explicitly.
The generated permissive corpus includes both sync spellings and a nonstandard
four-byte post-signature tag to keep that behavior exercised by native
`rastertopwg` and by `Translate`.  For Apple streams, CUPS uses the same
big-endian page-header integers in both branches of its `UNIR`/`RINU` reader;
the `RINU` spelling does not trigger the generic PWG byte swap.  The generated
`RINU` fixture therefore keeps its page dimensions and resolution in network
byte order.
For duplex output, `ExpectedHeader` describes the first/front page.  The
qualifier checks sheet-back transforms only on odd zero-based page indexes
(one-based pages 2, 4, ...), using CUPS' `_cupsRasterInitPWGHeader` mapping;
front pages retain transforms `1/1`.
